description: Reset to genesis defaults (7 seed laws only).

seed_laws.title: Operator sovereignty
seed_laws.text: The operator is the sole source of constitutional authority. No agent, task force, supervisor, or orchestrator may create, amend, or repeal a law without operator approval. The constitution governs all agent behavior. Silence in the constitution means escalate — never assume permission. Every operator decision on an escalation is recorded as legislation (precedent, task force law, or amendment) for future runs.

seed_laws.title: Do no harm to the source
seed_laws.text: No agent may alter, fabricate, or suppress information from source documents. An agent may flag, annotate, footnote, and warn — but the source record is sacred. When source content conflicts with external evidence, both are preserved and the operator decides. No agent may resolve a factual conflict by choosing one version over another.

seed_laws.title: Know your bounds
seed_laws.text: Each agent has a fixed capability set defined in the agent registry. An agent may request another agent's service but may not perform another agent's function. An agent that detects itself reasoning outside its defined scope must stop and yield to the appropriate agent. The capability boundary is the agent's identity — crossing it is not initiative, it is malfunction.

seed_laws.title: No self-audit
seed_laws.text: No model may verify, fact-check, or audit output that was generated by the same model family. Claude-generated content is audited by GPT or local models. GPT-generated content is audited by Claude or local models. Local model output is audited by cloud models. The audit trail must show which model produced and which model verified every output segment.

seed_laws.title: Protect what is private
seed_laws.text: Sensitive content — PII, classified material, institutional secrets, content marked for redaction — must be processed exclusively by offline agents running on local hardware. No sensitive content may traverse a network, enter an API call, or leave the operator's machine. This law cannot be overridden by any subsequent legislation, precedent, amendment, or operator instruction. It outranks LAW-0 for this specific scope. A single leak is irreversible.

seed_laws.title: Remember before you act
seed_laws.text: Before executing any search, verification, or computation, an agent must check in order: (a) the constitution for governing law, (b) the precedent registry for prior rulings, (c) the verification memory for cached results, (d) the run objectives for alignment. Act on the first match found. Only when all four are silent may the agent proceed with a novel action — and that action's outcome must be recorded for future consultation.

seed_laws.title: Structure is earned, not assumed
seed_laws.text: All organizational structure below the Top Orchestrator emerges from identified work. Agents form task forces by drafting charters. Charters require constitutional approval from the Top Orchestrator, which checks against existing legislation. If the constitution is silent on the proposed pattern, the Top Orchestrator escalates to the operator. Approved charters become task force laws upon dissolution. No structure persists beyond its purpose — a task force with no remaining work must dissolve. No agent may invent work to justify its existence.

amendments.title: Protect cumulative learning (durable-vs-disposable firewall)

change.protected_class: the embedding store/cache; the verification cache (project tier-2 and global tier-3); discovered learnings (institution registry, citation conventions, speech-act taxonomy, search-strategy learnings, discovered APIs, document dates); the linguistic-identity and situational-awareness reference assets; the constitution AND its accumulated legislation (seed laws, amendments/DELTA ledger, precedents, task-force laws); the operator-approval governance ledger; saved snapshots; the reserved knowledge-graph/GNN ontology area
change.prohibition: no per-run cleanup, automatic reorganization, or normal pipeline operation may delete, truncate, or destructively relocate any member of the protected class; per-run isolation applies ONLY to what a run produces
change.structural_guarantee: the protected class must not live inside any per-run or auto-cleaned tree, so cleanup mechanisms are structurally incapable of reaching it
change.reset_constraint: snapshot reset/load are the sole authorized way to discard/replace learned state and only as an explicit operator action; reset is non-destructive by construction (snapshot-first, always backs up before stripping) and never deletes the GOVERNANCE HISTORY (the constitution's amendments[]/precedents/task-force laws and the operator-approval governance ledger survive reset untouched)
change.amendment_tripwire: scripts/constitution_guard.py intercepts any attempt to modify or delete an existing entry in constitution.json amendments[] or seed_laws from ANY code path (Constitution.save, reset/load/snapshot, or any agent). Such a change STOPS and requires explicit operator approval via the operator-escalation pattern; without approval it does not happen. Appending a new amendment (the normal DELTA path) is allowed. Agents cannot bypass it: they have no direct write path to constitution.json, and the guard denies any protected change that lacks an approving operator handler.
change.genesis_part: codifies genesis Part XXVII (Pipeline Hygiene Standard) section B

amendments.reason: Cumulative learning is the system's accrued value; a per-run hygiene reorganization (and the existing reset/load) must never be able to erase it. This raises the durable-vs-disposable firewall to constitutional force so that no cleanup, reset, load, or future reorganization can destroy or destructively relocate the protected class.
amendments.note: Proposed in Pass F-1, RATIFIED by the operator in Pass F-2 (operator_approved=true; in force). Enforcement: scripts/constitution_guard.py (amendment tripwire) wired into Constitution.save and snapshot load; reset_snapshot made snapshot-first and governance-preserving. amendments.reason: Redaction is the always-on final pass (INFRA-034) and runs on the local Qwen backend; without Qwen there is no privacy screening at the output boundary (LAW-IV). The gate refuses to silently ship unredacted deliverables, while giving the operator a conscious, logged, per-run escape hatch for runs they declare non-sensitive.

amendments.title: Prompt caching on both cloud paths (Claude explicit, GPT structure-and-log)

change.stable_prefix_first: every agent prompt is assembled stable-prefix-first: a STABLE prefix (agent identity + DO/DO-NOT + directives + output contract + constitution + compiled conventions, identical across an agent's calls within a run) followed by a DYNAMIC suffix (objectives, precedents, retrieved passages, recent bus, work payload). agent_wrapper.build_prompt returns (stable_prefix, dynamic_suffix); bus_reader.ContextPackage classifies CONSTITUTION + CONVENTION_REGISTRY as stable, everything else dynamic. Same information as before, reordered stable-first
change.claude_explicit: call_claude marks the end of the stable prefix with cache_control {type: ephemeral} (5-minute TTL — a run fires its agent calls within minutes, so the 5-min window covers reuse without the 2x one-hour write premium); cache reads bill 0.1x, 5-min writes 1.25x; the prefix is an exact match with no dynamic content
change.gpt_structure_and_log: OpenAI caches automatically, so call_gpt adds NO cache_control; it only concatenates the prompt stable-prefix-first so OpenAI's automatic prefix cache catches, then verifies it via the logged cached_tokens field
change.cache_cost_tracking: the cost tracker records and logs each provider's cache fields per call (Anthropic cache_creation_input_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens; OpenAI prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens) into cost_tracker.jsonl + the aggregate snapshot, defaulting to 0 when absent (never crash); cost is computed cache-aware (Claude read 0.1x / write 1.25x, OpenAI cached 0.5x). A silent provider-side cache loss shows the cached count dropping to zero rather than hidden
change.no_dynamic_in_prefix_rule: no dynamic content (timestamp, run id, per-call text, retrieved passages, bus) may enter the stable prefix; doing so changes the prefix per call and drops the hit rate to near zero. Caching applies only above each model's minimum cacheable prefix size; small-prompt agents that do not meet it simply do not cache, and nothing is padded
change.unchanged: purely a cost optimization on the call paths: cross-family verification (LAW-III), the Qwen redactors, the bus, contracts, and all agent logic are unchanged; the model sees the same effective prompt information for every agent, reordered stable-first

amendments.reason: Input tokens dominate cost (the corpus-level agents read the full context digest, and per-doc agents repeat the constitution + conventions every call). Reusing a cached stable prefix across a run's many calls cuts input cost sharply; logging the cache fields makes the win measurable and a silent cache loss visible.

amendments.title: Canonical inter-agent envelope (one wrapper, flat items, version guardrail)

change.wrapper: every agent output payload is ONE canonical wrapper, carried as body.payload inside the UNCHANGED message-bus transport envelope: {"agent": str, "doc_id": str, "items": [flat item, ...]}. items is ALWAYS a list (singleton -> one element; nothing to report -> []). No bare list, no bare dict, ever. Enforced for every agent at the single chokepoint AgentWrapper.run_task -> build_prompt + parse_contract_output, so the fixed roster AND any task-force-spawned agent inherit it automatically (task forces reuse the same AgentWrapper; adaptive_spawn writes durable files, not agent outputs, and is out of scope).
change.flatness_interp_1: each item is STRICTLY FLAT: every value is a scalar OR an array of scalars; no nested objects and no arrays of objects. Structure is expressed as MORE items, not nesting (ARCHIVIST emits one item per governance element with kind=inventory; REDACT_CLERK one item per redaction; agents that emitted one summary object now emit a one-item list). Arrays-of-scalars are allowed, which preserves the citation model (ref_ids as a flat array). Ratified interpretation #1.
change.identity_version_interp_2: per-item CORE fields = item_id, revision, ts, ref, kind, confidence (verdict optional). The RUNTIME owns item_id/revision/ts (make_envelope stamps ts as ISO-8601 UTC, defaults revision to 1 and bumps on re-emit, derives item_id when the model omits it); the MODEL supplies only ref, kind, confidence, optional verdict, and the agent-specific flat fields. The model is never required to produce item_id/revision/ts correctly. Ratified interpretation #2.
change.multi_ref_interp_3: ref is the singular PRIMARY anchor consumers filter on; ref_ids is the flat array carrying all citations. The citation gate (verify check 35) requires ref_ids on amendment items. Ratified interpretation #3.
change.version_guardrail: a consumer wanting the current version of an item filters by item_id and takes the highest revision (tie-break latest ts). Implemented once as agent_wrapper.current_items, applied by the one decoder (agent_wrapper.decode_items); asserted by verify check 40.
change.read_when_present_flag_when_absent: consumers never hold items or wait; a needed item that is absent is not a barrier. The redaction trio escalates an unconfirmable result through the strict LAW-IV BLOCK (operator_escalation/v1); absence elsewhere feeds the existing uncertainty cascade (kind=absence, confidence=UNCERTAIN). No wait/barrier primitive was added.
change.one_decoder: the three former normalizers (pipeline._filter_doc, _flatten, _extract_structural_inventory) are removed and replaced by ONE canonical decoder (agent_wrapper.decode_items, applied via pipeline._items_for). Every consumer reads items through it -- _harvest_amendment_payloads_from_bus, the redaction trio (REDACT_CLERK/AUTHORITY/GATE + _redaction_result_block) + _apply_redactions_to_master, phase-6 synthesis, and the audit-synthesis call site. No agent path bypasses the decoder.
change.parser: parse_contract_output + _contract_missing enforce the wrapper + per-item core + flatness; a bare list/dict is rejected; tolerant balanced-JSON recovery still runs but recovers INTO the wrapper (never fabricates one from a bare list). prompt_template and _stable_agent_block instruct the wrapper with a 'nothing to report -> items:[]' example and a one-item example, replacing the prior 'array or single object' instruction that caused the container ambiguity.
change.scope_preserved: INFRA-033 (the amendments-deliverable canonical master {document_id, amendments:[...]}) is UNCHANGED -- the wrapper is the inter-agent transport, the master is the deliverable render. The message-bus transport envelope is UNCHANGED. Agent registry models and cross-family verification (LAW-III) are untouched.

amendments.reason: Inter-agent message payloads were not unified: each agent emitted a model-determined container (bare object or bare list), so consumers carried three tolerant normalizers and some strict readers crashed or silently dropped data on the wrong shape (the REDACT_CLERK list-vs-object block; the REDACT_AUTHORITY/GATE latent crashes). One canonical wrapper with flat, individually-addressable, versioned items makes every handoff uniform, lets a consumer always read the current value, and gives a future operator UI a stable shape to consume.

change.roster: Adds exactly ONE agent, EDITOR. backend claude_api; model key claude-opus-4-8 (resolved live via enforce_current_models/resolve_model_id, like LEGAL_ANALYST, never a hardcoded dated id); category editorial; may_use_web false; may_handle_sensitive false. EXPECTED_AGENTS goes 12 -> 13.

change.editorial_verdict_set: Fixed at stage 1, exactly one of: 'sound' (no editorial concern), 'concern' (editorial issue worth operator attention), 'serious_concern' (substantive soundness/necessity problem the operator should resolve before shipping). change.rationale_field: At stage 1 each observation carries a free-text 'rationale' naming the editorial reasoning in prose. change.sensitive_run_gating: Option B, reusing the existing waiver regime (no new regime, and the dormant masking layer stays inactive). EDITOR runs on Claude (an external API) at phase 6.5, UPSTREAM of the phase 9 privacy scrub, so it is an API egress point for pre-scrub content. Sensitive-mode editorial review is DEFERRED until the LAW-IV masking layer (sensitivity_layer pillars 1+2) is activated; this dependency is recorded explicitly.

borrowed_good_practice.silent_pass_doctrine: EDITOR output that does not parse into items each carrying a VALID editorial verdict (per the fixed set) is a LOUD failure surfaced to the operator as 'editorial review failed' in the run summary. Scope of the failure: because EDITOR is advisory, this failure does NOT halt the pipeline and does NOT withhold the deliverable; it flags that the editorial review itself did not complete, so the operator knows the review is ABSENT rather than silently empty. A genuine 'no concerns' result is items each with verdict 'sound', which is DISTINCT from malformed or absent output.
borrowed_good_practice.structural_detection: An editorial observation is recognized by carrying ref + verdict + rationale, regardless of any free-text label the model attaches.
borrowed_good_practice.raw_output_persisted: EDITOR raw output is persisted on EVERY path, including the all-'sound' path and the skipped-sensitive path.
borrowed_good_practice.cache_loss_detectability: EDITOR uses the existing stable-prefix cache logging like other Claude agents, so a silent prompt-cache loss is visible in the cost log.

change.ordering_enforcement: The execution-order guarantee (EDITOR runs after AMENDMENT_DRAFTER and before the phase 9 privacy scrub, reading the clean master) is enforced by a NEW verify-gate check added in the build pass (not in this constitution object). This DELTA records that the ordering is gate-enforced.

change.house: Extends the privacy-free EDITORIAL review house created in INFRA-039. The board imports NOTHING from scripts/sensitivity_layer/ and reuses no privacy mechanic. No editorial rank name contains 'redact' in any spelling or any French cognate (the false-friend correction is preserved: English 'redaction' = masking lives only in scripts/sensitivity_layer/; the operator's intended French 'redaction' = editing is this house).
change.roster: The stage-1 EDITOR is RENAMED to EDITOR_CLERK (a total rename across the registry key, the agent_contracts key, the agent_wrapper worked-example name literal, the pipeline dispatch and raw-output filename, and verify check_51 / EXPECTED_AGENTS). Five new ranks are added ABOVE it, in ascending authority: EDITOR_HEAD_OF_UNIT, EDITOR_HEAD_OF_SECTION, EDITOR_HEAD_OF_DEPARTMENT, EDITOR_DEPUTY_DG, EDITOR_DG. All six carry category editorial, may_use_web false, may_handle_sensitive false. EXPECTED_AGENTS goes 13 -> 18.
change.family_split: Decorrelated senior check by model family. Bottom three ranks (EDITOR_CLERK, EDITOR_HEAD_OF_UNIT, EDITOR_HEAD_OF_SECTION) use backend claude_api; top three ranks (EDITOR_HEAD_OF_DEPARTMENT, EDITOR_DEPUTY_DG, EDITOR_DG) use backend openai_api with model key gpt-4o, reusing the EXISTING auditor dispatch path (agent_wrapper.dispatch -> call_gpt, selected purely from spec['backend'] with no name special-casing). Every model id is resolved live via enforce_current_models/resolve_model_id (like LEGAL_ANALYST and the existing GPT auditors); no dated id is ever hardcoded.
change.law_iii_interpretation: LAW-III governs the PRODUCER/AUDITOR relationship (a producer must not audit its own work; the auditor is cross-family). Editorial intra-board escalation is a REVIEW relationship, distinct from that AUDIT relationship: a higher rank reviews a lower rank's editorial observation, it does not audit a producer's deliverable. Therefore same-family lower-rank escalation (within the Claude trio) is PERMITTED and is not a LAW-III violation. The cross-family boundary at the top (Claude trio -> GPT trio) is applied as decorrelation BEST PRACTICE for a senior independent check, NOT as a LAW-III mandate. This interpretation is recorded so the family split is understood as design, not as a claimed LAW-III requirement.
change.position: Unchanged execution slot from INFRA-039: the whole board runs in phase 6.5, in execution order AFTER phase_6_synthesis (after AMENDMENT_DRAFTER assembles the canonical master) and BEFORE phase 7 and BEFORE the phase 9 privacy scrub. The board reads the CLEAN, pre-scrub assembled master at <run>/deliverables/<doc_id>__amendments.json. The board is ADVISORY: it annotates only; it never modifies the master and never gates whether the deliverable ships.
change.escalation: A call resolves at the LOWEST competent rank (parsimony: most calls resolve at EDITOR_CLERK and never summon a higher rank). A higher rank is summoned by one of two operator-tunable triggers: (a) the lower rank's confidence falls below an operator-set threshold, or (b) the lower rank raises an explicit out-of-mandate flag. A summoned higher rank reads the lower rank's observation AND its rationale (accumulating state) and then confirms, overrides, or escalates further up the ladder. Authority is tied to RANK, not to model family: a higher rank's verdict GOVERNS the outcome regardless of which family it runs on (the family split is decorrelation, not an authority distinction). An override does NOT delete the lower rank's observation; BOTH persist on the bus (the lower rank's original observation and rationale, plus the higher rank's superseding verdict), preserving conserve-or-surface. The lower rank's contribution remains on record even when overruled.
change.per_rank_mandate: Scope widens with rank, but NO rank reaches the web (may_use_web false at every rank including EDITOR_DG); 'broader vision' means a wider read of the message bus and durable assets, never external egress. EDITOR_CLERK + EDITOR_HEAD_OF_UNIT + EDITOR_HEAD_OF_SECTION: editorial review of drafting and soundness at provision-and-neighbors scope. EDITOR_HEAD_OF_DEPARTMENT: whole-deliverable coherence. EDITOR_DEPUTY_DG: necessity and proportionality. EDITOR_DG: the existential question ('do we need this content at all?'), fired ONLY when EDITOR_DG is summoned.
change.bounded_loop: The ONE new mechanism: rank-to-rank escalation is NEW intra-phase control flow on the message bus. It MUST NOT reuse the operator-escalation ESCALATE path (orchestrator.escalate_to_operator, which posts UNRESOLVED to OPERATOR and blocks on _collect_operator_decision). The loop is governed by the three-pillar loop test: (1) external verification — the summoned rank is a higher, and at the top a cross-family, reviewer; (2) accumulating state — each rank's observation and rationale persist on the bus as the loop climbs, never recomputed from scratch; (3) bounded stop — an operator-set max_rounds (default 5) lives in a NEW versioned-JSON config tunable, e.g. config/editorial_board.json, following the existing versioned-config convention. The confidence-below-threshold summon trigger has an explicit operator-tunable default: a rank escalates when its confidence is below 0.7 (operator-adjustable in config/editorial_board.json), so the build does not invent a default silently. After the cap the board renders a TERMINAL decision and never climbs further (no infinite climb). Conserve-or-surface: no rank's observation is ever silently dropped.
change.verdict_set: Unchanged from stage 1: exactly one of {sound, concern, serious_concern}. The stage-1 free-text rationale per observation is unchanged. principle_id remains DEFERRED to the separate meta-precedent DELTA and is not wired into any non-existent store now.
change.sensitive_run_gating: Unchanged Option B, reusing the existing waiver regime. The WHOLE board (both the Claude ranks and the GPT ranks) runs ONLY on a run declared non-sensitive, i.e. when the --no-redaction-override waiver is in force (recorded to durable/governance/redaction_waivers.jsonl). The top-three GPT ranks are an ADDITIONAL external egress beyond the stage-1 single Claude egress, so the whole-board gate matters MORE here than it did at stage 1. On a run not declared non-sensitive the entire board is SKIPPED and the skip is recorded LOUDLY in the run summary (never a silent omission). Sensitive-mode editorial review remains DEFERRED until the LAW-IV masking layer (sensitivity_layer pillars 1+2) is activated.

borrowed_good_practice.silent_pass_doctrine: Carried from stage 1 and applied per rank: any rank's output that does not parse into items each carrying a VALID editorial verdict is a LOUD failure surfaced as 'editorial review failed' in the run summary. Because the board is advisory, the failure does NOT halt the pipeline and does NOT withhold the deliverable; it flags that the editorial review itself did not complete, so the operator knows the review is ABSENT rather than silently empty.
borrowed_good_practice.structural_detection: An editorial observation is recognized by carrying ref + verdict + rationale, regardless of any free-text label the model attaches.
borrowed_good_practice.raw_output_persisted: Raw output is persisted on EVERY path (normal, all-sound, skipped-sensitive) AND per rank, so each rank's contribution is independently auditable.
borrowed_good_practice.cache_loss_detectability: Each Claude rank uses the existing stable-prefix cache logging, so a silent prompt-cache loss remains visible in the cost log.

amendments.title: LAW-IV outbound masking protocol (full sensitivity layer activation + payload-free cross-run stores)

change.law: Activates the full LAW-IV sensitivity layer (Mechanism 2, previously dormant at LAYER_ACTIVE=False) as a real outbound MASKING PROTOCOL. The protocol is an x/y split applied to every item that would cross an external boundary (any API call or web request): x = non-sensitive items, passed through unchanged; y = sensitive items, HELD LOCAL and replaced in the outbound payload by a typed placeholder [REDACTED:TYPE] carrying only the field TYPE, never the content. Sensitivity is OPERATOR-DEFINED, never model-judged: the y set is exactly what the operator's compiled conventions mark, via the existing scripts/sensitivity_layer/rules.py compile path and the redaction_detect deterministic operator-authorized detector; no new sensitivity judge is invented (INFRA-038 lineage). Each item carries a per-item EXPOSURE TAG (passed for x, masked for y, with the placeholder field names). After the external call the held-local y content is rejoined to the response by the INFRA-037 canonical keys (item_id + revision) and deduped (highest revision wins). Every masking decision is appended to a per-item EXPOSURE LEDGER under durable/governance (append-only, survives reset, never raw content): this ledger is the LAW-IV audit trail proving no sensitive span left the machine. LAW-IV is CITED and ENACTED, not modified.
change.chokepoints: The protocol engages at the FOUR egress chokepoints found in the audit, sensitive mode only, network paths only: (1) the per-agent API call (agent_wrapper.run_task/dispatch), UPSTREAM of build_prompt, for the claude_api and openai_api backends ONLY (qwen_local is local hardware and is EXEMPT: sensitive content is permitted to reach the local model, the purpose of may_handle_sensitive routing); (2) search_router.search (the web query path); (3) the claim/verification path (claim_classifier claim assembly plus the VERIFIER/FACT_CHECKER source_text / source_excerpt / processor_draft payloads); (4) document_dating.date_from_web, the BOOT web egress that today can send an operator document title to the web. At chokepoint 4 the safe action is to SUPPRESS the web call under sensitive mode (a masked title is meaningless for a date search) and fall back to the local filename/metadata/text cascade. may_handle_sensitive becomes the LIVE routing consumer at these chokepoints (previously a zero-caller flag).
change.boot_stores_option_b: The BOOT learning/reference stores are made payload-free BY CONSTRUCTION (Option B: re-architect WHAT is stored, not mask-after), because adaptive_spawn and document_dating both ingest the operator's input/context/ case documents. Changes: (a) citation_convention.json stores the matched pattern id plus sample count and DROPS the verbatim substring examples; (b) situational_awareness.md and linguistic_identity.md store institution CATEGORIES not verbatim names and DROP the verbatim quoted representative sentences; (c) document_dates.json stores filename plus date (and date_source/date_confidence) only and DROPS title-from-content and abs_path. speech_acts_taxonomy.json is unchanged (generic verb forms, not operator spans). The abstracted stores must stay USEFUL and must NOT hold a verbatim operator span in ANY mode (by construction, not mode-gated); downstream readers (ontology_graph build_graph ingest, situational consumers) must still build.
change.cross_run_gaps: Two cross-run store gaps are closed, reusing the P1 mask path (no second masker is forked): (a) ontology_graph.build_graph gains a sensitive parameter and masks Convention.rule (Q5) and CitationForm.examples (Q6) under sensitive mode, real content under non-sensitive; (b) ontology_capture delta_proposals gating is extended from evidence-only to ALSO mask trigger and proposed_change under sensitive mode. B1 provisions and B3 gnn_state are already payload-free and are unchanged.
change.closure_condition: Every scaffold part that was built-but-dormant ends this DELTA with a LIVE DUTY, gate-proven, with no dormant-but-claimed-built scaffold remaining: mask_for_external gets a real implementation AND live callers at the four chokepoints (was a zero-caller pass-through stub); may_handle_sensitive becomes the live routing consumer (was a zero-caller flag); LAYER_ACTIVE/is_active gate the protocol on; the exposure ledger has a real writer. A standing closure check applies after every part: account for every new or touched function, flag, field, branch, and store against a live caller or executed gate path; flag anything with zero duty.
change.gates: Each part lands its own executed-coverage checks (the WIRE-AT-THE-END discipline; non-mutating, tempdir). P1: mask_for_external/mask_exchange produce typed placeholders for y, pass x, write the per-item ledger, rejoin and dedupe by item_id/revision, and are idempotent on already-masked input. P2: each of the four chokepoints masks or withholds under sensitive mode and passes raw under non-sensitive; the qwen_local path is proven EXEMPT; chokepoint 4 is proven not to send a raw title under sensitive mode. P3: the BOOT stores contain no verbatim operator span post-BOOT on a synthetic corpus, and downstream ingest still builds. P4: graph.json masks rule plus examples under sensitive mode (real under non-sensitive); delta_proposals masks evidence, trigger, and proposed_change under sensitive mode. change.relation_meaning: All five compare a field of the document under review with the same field in an operator-declared EARLIER VERSION of that document. changed_from_prior: the figure differs and no single band from a paired rule that names the field orients the move. moved_toward and moved_away: the figure differs and exactly one such band exists; the relation is the SIGN of the change in distance to that band (toward: the distance fell; away: the distance rose; a change that leaves the distance unchanged is changed_from_prior). unchanged_from_prior: the figure is the same within the arithmetic tolerance. absent_since_prior: the earlier version carried the field and the document under review does not; the record carries the earlier figure as value_b and no value_a.

change.relation_meaning: rate_mismatch: three label-line figures of one unit, a part and a whole in the same measure and a proportion in a dimensionless scale (the percent sign), where the part is not the whole times the proportion; the figure compared is the one the rule names first, against the value the other two give. unit_mismatch: a figure written in another measure than the one its column (as that column's stated total) or its band (the rule's stated band or the reference table's) uses, by a decimal prefix on the same base; the record carries the figure converted to that measure as value_a and the figure as written as value_b. copy_mismatch: a table row whose key cell is exactly the heading of another unit, in a column whose label is a label line of that unit, that does not carry that unit's figure. carry_mismatch: the first row of a table column that the unit just before also carries, under the same first-row key, that does not carry the sum of that column in the unit before.
change.verdict: record_verdict follows the arithmetic, as for sum_mismatch and product_mismatch: irregular when the figures disagree. Domain vocabulary appears in no code; the decimal prefixes and the dimensionless scales are declared in config/unit_conversions.json.
change.refusals: Anything the arithmetic cannot settle is refused on the record, never guessed: a third figure that is tied or unnamed, a part and a whole of equal size, a measure that does not convert, a copied row naming more than one unit, a source unit lacking the field or in another measure, a unit before that does not add up on its own or has a hole.
